quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: Handlebars should be ______ the rider's seat.

options.text: No more than 10 inches higher than
No more than 25 inches higher than

questions.correctAnswerText: No more than 25 inches higher than
questions.explanation: Motorcycle handlebars cannot be more than 25 inches above the rider's seat.

questions.question: When riding with a group of motorcyclists, a staggered formation:

options.text: Should not be used when entering or exiting a highway.
Should be used when riding in curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be used when entering or exiting a highway.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is generally good, but groups should switch to single-file when riding in curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger on your motorcycle, you should tell the passenger to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before the engine starts.
Sit as far back as possible on the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not talk or move unnecessarily.
questions.explanation: Tell passengers to avoid talking or moving while the motorcycle is moving. Passengers should get on only after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the rider.

questions.question: When passing a truck on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Not return to your original lane until you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
Return to your original lane as soon as the truck is behind you.
Return to your original lane when you feel you have enough space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not return to your original lane until you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Only return to your original lane when you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic or pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head, shoulders, and torso.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: Look through every turn by turning just your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: You approach an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with its lights flashing. You should:

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle begins moving again.
Merge into a lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge into a lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you approach an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space and proceed with caution. Always slow down and be ready to stop near an emergency scene.

questions.question: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should:

options.text: Create an angle with the curb that is between 45 and 90 degrees.
Be parked without a wheel or fender touching the curb.
Be parked parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Create an angle with the curb that is between 45 and 90 degrees.
questions.explanation: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should create an angle with the curb between 45 and 90 degrees. A wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: When you are being passed on the left, you should:

options.text: Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed on your left, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the right can be dangerous because it may cause the passing driver to re-enter your lane too quickly.

questions.question: Using all three lane positions is:

options.text: Not encouraged because then you can never get used to any part of a lane.
Discouraged because it confuses other motorists.
Wise if you are adapting to changing conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wise if you are adapting to changing conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that the road ahead will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:
questions.correctAnswerText: In broad daylight.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials when riding, even during daylight.

questions.question: When turning a curve while riding in a group, you should be in:
questions.correctAnswerText: A single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Groups normally ride in a staggered formation. Switch to single-file when turning a curve, making a turn, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride more slowly than the speed limit.
Cover the clutch and the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and the brakes.
questions.explanation: When approaching an intersection, cover both the clutch and brakes. This reduces reaction time if you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that traffic ahead will merge.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To avoid a hazard, press gently on the handgrip on the side where you want to escape.

questions.question: Helmets are:

options.text: Only required for inexperienced motorcycle users.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear a DOT-approved helmet every time they ride. A helmet is the best protection against head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Provide a narrow view of the road behind you.
Provide a wide view of the road behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show more of the road behind you than flat mirrors. They make objects appear farther away than they really are. Take time to adjust to convex mirrors if your motorcycle has them.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help you maintain control while turning?
questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate through the turn.
questions.explanation: To turn safely, slow down before entering the turn. Look through the turn in the direction you want to go. Lean your body into the turn and gently increase throttle through the turn to stabilize the suspension.

questions.question: When riding at night, keep a minimum following distance of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: At night, it is hard to judge how far away other vehicles are. Stay at least three seconds behind the vehicle in front of you.
